## {{< fa solid dna >}} About
[**Verónica Andreo**](https://veroandreo.gitlab.io/) is a biologist. She holds a PhD in
Biological Sciences and an MSc in Remote Sensing and GIS applications.
She works as a researcher for [CONICET](https://www.conicet.gov.ar/) and lecturer at the
[Gulich Institute](http://ig.conae.unc.edu.ar/) — Argentinian Space Agency
[(CONAE)](https://www.argentina.gob.ar/ciencia/conae) in Córdoba, Argentina.
Her research focuses on applications of spatial information and geotechnologies to problems
related to the ecology of zoonotic and vector-borne diseases and public health.
Specifically, she works on uncovering **environmental drivers of vector-borne disease
distribution and outbreaks**, with a particular interest in those environmental features
that can be derived **by means of satellite image analysis, remote sensing time series
and GIS-based techniques**.

Verónica is part of the [**GRASS GIS**](https://grass.osgeo.org/) project and has served
as coordinator of the [development team](https://grass.osgeo.org/about/team/) since 2021.
She is a strong advocate for free and open source software for geospatial (FOSS4G) and a
member of [OSGeo](https://www.osgeo.org/), the Open Source Geospatial Foundation.
She was the Program Committee chair for the international conference
[**FOSS4G 2021**](2021.foss4g.org/), hosted by Argentina.
Among other activities, she has volunteered as a mentor for GRASS GIS in the
[Google Code-In](https://codein.withgoogle.com/) contest, introducing high school students
to the open source world, and in
[Google Summer of Code](https://summerofcode.withgoogle.com/)
for university students and developers.
:::
